title: Hot chocolate / cocoa, dry mix, made with water, with whipped cream

content.title: About
content.content: A dry mix for hot chocolate / cocoa is designed for quick preparation by simply adding hot water. The blend usually contains cocoa powder, sugar, powdered milk and flavorings. It is often topped with whipped cream, giving the drink a creamy texture and rich taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dry mixes appeared in the early 20th century when cocoa powder began to be produced on an industrial scale.
In Russia, hot chocolate gained popularity after ready‑made mixes appeared in stores in the 1990s.
Whipped cream as a topping makes the drink more caloric but also more aromatic.
The cocoa powder used in mixes often undergoes Dutch processing, which removes most of the caffeine and theobromine.
Emulsifiers are sometimes added to help the cream stay on the surface.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa is rich in flavonoids that combat free radicals and support vascular health.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Caffeine and theobromine can boost serotonin levels and improve mood.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The mix typically provides magnesium, iron and calcium, important for muscles and bones.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Sugar and quick‑acting carbohydrates give an immediate energy lift, useful in cold weather.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Many mixes are fortified with vitamins B1, B2 and B6, which play roles in metabolism.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Adding whipped cream significantly raises the drink’s calorie count.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The mix often contains powdered milk, which may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or casein allergy.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: For caffeine‑sensitive individuals, drinking hot chocolate in the evening may disturb sleep.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour 200‑250 ml of hot water over the mix, stir thoroughly until smooth, then add a dollop of whipped cream. You can garnish with grated chocolate, cinnamon or vanilla sugar. Serve hot in a mug.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the dry mix in a sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, use within 3‑6 months. Store whipped cream separately in the refrigerator and add just before serving.
